about: S3b (RC-R10-15, RC-R10-16): how donor features transfer to a host. Covering extents with a reason per donor covering ('Class:covering' overrides 'covering'), anchors by slot (RC-R10-14), and identity cues for discrete parts ('Class:part'; positive wording only). A part without a cue gets one derived from its class_parts shape with the placement words removed. Model-estimated, reviewed by the engineer; the extents follow the donor's own body, never one reviewed image.

exoskeleton.reason: RC-R10-16: an exoskeleton is a whole-body system, plates on every segment and limb section; the face keeps the host's own skin so the eyes, nose and mouth stay readable

Mammalia:scales.reason: as on the donor: overlapping scales cover the crown, back, flanks, outer limbs and tail, and the belly and face stay soft-skinned

scales.reason: as on the donor: scales cover the whole body

Reptilia:shell.reason: as on the donor: the shell covers the trunk, and the neck, legs and tail stay free to move

shell.reason: as on the donor: the shell covers the back
